rows.details: NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad (NALSAR) in partnership with ALPN Research Foundation, Bengaluru (ALPN)
A Scoping Report on Broiler Chicken Welfare in India
Across six states in India (Field research across approximately 60 farm visits, slaughterhouses, and meat shops)

content_sections.heading: About NALSAR Project Lead
content_sections.text: NALSAR University of Law is an institution that aims to provide quality legal education underlining constitutionalism, rule of law, and justice, with a focus on social justice for marginalised communities. In this initiative, NALSAR is partnering with the ALPN Research Foundation, a not-for-profit independent think-tank working towards improving animal welfare across India. Together, they are undertaking a study that systematically assesses current conditions and challenges to the welfare of broiler chickens in India from end-to-end, including farming systems, supply chains, market demand, regulatory context, and the broader stakeholder ecosystem.

content_sections.heading: Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The recruitment notification offers a total of 1 position for the Project Lead role under the study titled ‘A Scoping Report on Broiler Chicken Welfare in India’. content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Candidates must meet the following qualification requirements: Demonstrated subject-matter expertise in broiler chicken production in India with a background in veterinary science, animal husbandry, poultry science, or a closely related technical field is strongly preferred. Strong working knowledge of broiler farming systems in India (backyard, contract farming, integrated commercial operations) and common welfare issues within them. Familiarity with animal welfare science and assessment frameworks as applied to broiler chickens. Prior field experience visiting or working directly with poultry farms, ideally in rural or semi-urban India, would be an asset. Fluency in English required; proficiency in regional languages would be an asset for fieldwork.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: This is a six-month-long, full-time research role. Field research is expected to take place for three months across approximately 60 farm visits in six states, plus slaughterhouses and meat shops. All fieldwork costs will be covered by the organisation.

content_sections.heading: NALSAR Project Lead Job Description
content_sections.text: The Project Lead will be responsible for the following duties and tasks as outlined in the project notification: Lead technical research and analysis on broiler farming systems in India – production practices, housing, breeds and genetics, feeding regimes, health management, and welfare conditions across different system types (backyard, contract, integrated, and commercial). Design and execute a fieldwork plan covering approximately 60 farm visits across six states, plus slaughterhouses and meat retail points, assessing on-ground farming practices and welfare conditions firsthand. Conduct and synthesise literature on broiler production and welfare in India. Build relationships with farmers, veterinarians, and production-side stakeholders to support fieldwork and ongoing insight-gathering. Assess the nature and extent of animal welfare across various farming systems, and evaluate the malleability of each system to welfare-improving interventions. Provide subject-matter expertise on technical sections of the final report (industry overview, farming systems analysis) and contribute broiler-specific expertise to cross-cutting insights. Identify and prioritise a list of potential welfare-focused interventions based on technical feasibility and likely adoption by relevant stakeholders. Coordinate with the wider research team (who will lead economic, market, and regulatory analysis) to ensure technical findings feed into the overall report.
